current.text: He has a torn labrum in his shoulder. He is expected to miss about five to six months, which puts his return around mid to late March.
Do not draft him and do not stash him on IL.
While he is out, Ighodaro and Maluach split the center minutes. Ighodaro has started two games in a row over Maluach, and their minutes are similar.
Even when healthy, he is expected to lose the starting job to Maluach and play about 16 to 17 minutes a night as a backup big.
He re-signed with Phoenix for 3 years and 38 million, about 13 million a year.
Ben thinks the contract was signed mainly so Phoenix can trade him at the deadline or in a year.

durable.text: He is a low-usage big man. His value comes from a high FG%, good FT% for a center, and rebounds. He is not a big shot blocker.
His high FG% is a league outlier and lifts a team's FG% clearly.
He plays around the rim and makes no threes.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.
He does not play enough games. Even with load management, minutes limits and skipped back-to-backs, he played only 60 games last season.

note: He is out with a torn labrum until about mid to late March. Our season ends 2027-03-28, so at best he returns for the last playoff week, and Ben projects him as a 16 to 17 minute backup behind Maluach when he does. That is why Yahoo (rank 206, about 1 USD average cost) and ESPN (rank 313, 0 USD) barely price him, well below the 9 USD he cost in our league last year. Do not spend an auction dollar or an IL slot on him. When healthy he is a strong FG% and rebounds center for punt 3PM builds, so if his rehab moves ahead of schedule, check the waiver wire and the center split between Ighodaro and Maluach in Phoenix.
